the CD38+ T cell population is a mixture of naive and activated memory T cells and that the CD38+/HLA-DR+ population is largely a population of activated memory T cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune activation in the context of HIV infection is not only associated with a higher mortality but also with the risk for developing a non-AIDS-defining cancer (NADC).
we found a significant association between CD8 + T-cell HLA-DR expression and risk of death, and no association between CD38 + H LA-DR + T-cell frequency and risk of death.
the T-cell activation marker CD38, when measured by relative fluorescence, is not a prognostic marker in the era of ART.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD38 is not a useful marker of T-cell activation during ART-suppressed HIV infection.
CD8 + T-cell activation is a powerful predictor of mortality in treated HIV infection and that CD4 + T-cell activation may also be a useful predictor.
